texts.preamble: Smt.Urvi Piramal & 2 Ors. vs State Of M.P. & Ors.
texts.facts: The petitioners before this Court have filed present petition under Sec.482 of Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of complaint pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Indore filed by the respondent No.1 for offences under Sec.7(i), 14(a) read with Sec.16(1)(a)(i) and 16(1)(c) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The petitioners' contention is that as per the case of prosecution Shri Sachin Logaria, Food Inspector visited the shop of the petitioners on 29/11/2007 and took samples of 'Jaora Gold Rawa' and 'Best Choice Besan'. In respect of Porridge (Rawa), the date of packing was October, 2007 and for Gram Flour (Besan) the date of packing was November 2007. The best before date provided on the pouch in case of Porridge was 60 days from the date of packing and in case of Gram Flour it was 3 months from the date of packing. A memo was drawn in Form No.IV under Rule 12 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. The petitioners have further stated that Porridge and Gram Flour was sent for analysis and a report from Laboratory was obtained on 14/12/2007. The petitioners have further stated that for the first time vide letter dated 29/12/2008 which was actually received by the petitioners on 15/01/2009. The report was forwarded to the petitioner on 15/01/2009 and the petitioner for the first time came to know about the report and the prosecution on 15/01/2009.
texts.arguments: The petitioners have further stated that the products were also packed in pouches and each pouch was printed with the date of manufacture of product in question, the best before date and the name of manufacturer was also very much in existence. Learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that once the shelf life of the sample seized was over, the question of making a request by the petitioner for reanalysis does not arise and in light of the judgment delivered by this Court in the case of Prahlad Gattani and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2012(4) MPLJ 617. Hence, the entire complaint itself deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned counsel for the petitioner has also placed reliance upon the judgment of apex Court delivered in the case of Rameshwar Dayal Vs. State of U.P. reported in 1995 Supp (4) SCC 659 and the apex Court has taken a similar view in the matter. Learned counsel has also placed reliance upon a judgment delivered in the case of Ram Singh Vs. State of M. P. reported in 2005(3) MPLJ 458 wherein this Court has also taken a similar view. Lastly reliance has been placed upon a judgment delivered in the case of Venkateshwaran Narayanan Ayyar and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2006(2) MPLJ 592 and it has been argued that the petitioners were not responsible for the conduct of the business of the Company who has manufactured Porridge and Gram Flour and therefore, no case is made out against them.
